transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we have a confirmed molded-housing order and we're short on our usual resin. R-19 is available as a possible temporary substitute, and Lines 5 and 6 can normally mold the housing. Before I make any decision on whether to authorize this campaign, we need to do our ten-minute readiness huddle per plant procedure. I need to hear from quality, process maintenance, materials planning, and EHS on any concerns or conditions with running R-19 on Lines 5 or 6. Let's get started — who wants to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share something important: I obtained the customer's signed deviation waiver this morning. It specifies that only resin R-19 from lot 44B may be used, and the campaign requires 20 first-off housings for dimensional inspection plus 5 tensile-test specimens. I have not attached the waiver to the production order yet.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share my compatibility findings from yesterday's maintenance inspection. Line 6's screw coating is incompatible with R-19, so Line 6 should not be used for this campaign. Line 5 is suitable, but only after a 2-hour purge and screen replacement. I confirmed this during yesterday's inspection but haven't entered it in the work-order system yet, so it wouldn't show up in our normal records. We'd need to schedule that purge and screen replacement before any R-19 run on Line 5.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share my materials planning findings. My inventory reconciliation shows exactly 780 kg of R-19 lot 44B available, and the approved material calculation is 0.65 kg per housing, which allows for exactly 1,200 housings. I have not posted the lot reservation yet because the alternate-material authorization is still pending. Evan, this aligns with your customer waiver specifying lot 44B — we have enough material for the campaign, but I'll hold the reservation until Marisol authorizes it.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to share my EHS findings on R-19. I reviewed R-19's handling sheet this week — I received the revised sheet from the resin supplier, and it requires grounded closed transfer and a hopper fill limit of 60 percent during the campaign. I have not yet updated the area work instruction to reflect these requirements, so the current work instruction on the floor does not include them. These controls need to be in place before we run R-19 on Line 5.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: Attach the customer's signed deviation waiver to the production order before the campaign begins.
Schedule and complete the 2-hour purge and screen replacement on Line 5 before any R-19 run, and enter the work-order record in the system.
Post the lot reservation for 780 kg of R-19 lot 44B after this authorization is granted.
Update the area work instruction to reflect R-19's grounded closed transfer requirement and 60 percent hopper fill limit before the campaign begins.
